stories.headline: ‘Other than occasional fights’: Argentina’s first Haiti-born U-17 player Kiki on racism claims
stories.deck: Liverpool have completed the £106 million signing of 23-year-old Bradley Barcola from PSG, with the deal potentially rising to £123 million. The French forward has signed a five-year contract and will wear No.29. A long-term Liverpool target, Barcola joins after winning two Champions League titles and three Ligue 1 crowns, aiming to win the Premier League.
stories.bodyText:
Kiki Ramos, the Haiti-born winger who recently became the first player born in the Caribbean country to represent Argentina, has pushed back against criticism surrounding racism and discrimination in Argentina, saying he has never personally experienced it since arriving in the country as a baby.
The 17-year-old made his Argentina U-17 debut this week in a 2-1 victory over Ecuador, marking a significant moment for a player whose journey to the Albiceleste began after the devastating earthquake that struck Haiti in January 2010.
Ramos was born in Haiti on April 3, 2009, and arrived in Argentina at nine months old after being adopted by an Argentine couple. He has since developed through Vélez Sarsfield and is now attracting attention from clubs in Europe.
Ramos responds to criticism surrounding Argentina
Amid criticism of Argentina and allegations of racism circulating on social media, Ramos gave his own account of his experience in the country. Speaking as quoted by Albiceleste Talk, he said:
"Did I feel any racism or discrimination in Argentina? Ever since I came to Argentina, I’ve never felt discriminated against.”
“Other than the occasional fights between youth players during matches, everything has always been fine off the pitch. 
I never felt discriminated against, and I never felt different from anyone else. That’s why I feel like people who say Argentina is racist are just saying it for the sake of it."
Ramos added:
"I think we’re just going through a period where Argentina is being heavily criticised, you know? But Argentina is a beautiful country. For me, it’s a dream to represent Argentina and a huge honour to wear this beautiful shirt. I’ve dreamed of it since I was a little kid, and I hope I can live up to it every time I’m called up.”
Ramos' remarkable journey to the Argentina shirt
Ramos, who goes by "Kiki", survived the 7.0-magnitude earthquake that devastated Haiti in January 2010. The disaster caused more than 100,000 deaths, with an official figure of 316,000 later provided by Haiti's government, according to the material surrounding his story.
After arriving in Argentina as a nine-month-old, Ramos was adopted by an Argentine family and eventually began his football development at Vélez Sarsfield. His emergence with the club has now taken him into Argentina's youth setup, where his debut came in the 2-1 win over Ecuador.
His appearance has also attracted attention because of the historical context around players born outside Argentina representing the national team. According to the reports, Ramos could become the first player without Argentine roots to play an official match for the senior Argentina side since Paraguayan-born Heriberto Correa represented the Albiceleste after becoming an Argentine citizen in 1973.
There is an unusual link between the two players beyond their birthplace circumstances: both arrived at Argentina's national-team setup while representing Vélez Sarsfield, although more than five decades separate their stories.
Ramos' next major opportunity could come with Argentina's U-17 side at the 2026 FIFA U-17 World Cup, which will be held in Qatar from November 19 to December 13.
For now, though, his focus is on building his career with Vélez and continuing to earn opportunities in Argentina's youth teams, while his comments offer a personal account that contrasts with the broader criticism surrounding the country and its football culture.

stories.headline: Liverpool finally get their man: $144M Barcola becomes second-most expensive signing
stories.deck: Liverpool have signed 23-year-old Bradley Barcola from PSG on a five-year contract for £106 million, potentially rising to £123 million. The France international, who won two Champions League titles and three Ligue 1 crowns with PSG, will wear No.29. A long-term Liverpool target, Barcola hopes to help the Reds win the Premier League and establish himself at Anfield.
stories.bodyText:
Liverpool have completed the signing of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain, with the 23-year-old forward joining the Reds on a long-term contract after passing his medical and completing the formalities of the transfer.
The deal is worth a guaranteed £106 million ($144m), according to ESPN sources, with a further £17m ($23m) available in performance-related add-ons. That makes Barcola the second-most-expensive signing in Liverpool's history, behind only Alexander Isak, who joined the club from Newcastle United for £125m last summer.
Barcola has signed a five-year contract and will wear the No.29 shirt at Anfield.
Speaking to Liverpoolfc.com after completing his move, Barcola said: "It's a great pride to be able to play for Liverpool. I'm very happy.
"It took a long time but I'm really happy today to be able to play for Liverpool and all I want is to be on the pitch and be able to play.
"I hope to achieve very big things. First of all, winning the Premier League – it's one of my biggest dreams in my life.
"It is to do that and to stay in this team in the long term – that's why I signed a long contract – and I hope I can do it."
Why Barcola chose Liverpool
Barcola had been a long-term Liverpool target and, according to ESPN sources, was unwilling to consider alternative destinations this summer as he pushed for a move away from PSG.
The France international had become an important part of PSG's recent success, making 152 appearances, scoring 39 goals and providing 35 assists during his three-year spell in Paris. He won back-to-back Champions League titles and three successive Ligue 1 crowns with the club.
His departure comes after competition for places at PSG prompted him to look for a new opportunity, with Liverpool offering him the chance to take on a major role in their attack.
Barcola had also previously played twice at Anfield and said those experiences helped convince him that Liverpool was the right destination.
"I had the chance to play twice in this stadium and I saw the atmosphere and how the fans were behind the Liverpool players.
"When I knew about Liverpool's interest in me, I didn't ask questions and I knew it was a very big club for me."
Barcola's career before Liverpool
Barcola began his senior career with Lyon, making his first-team debut in November 2021. He went on to make 47 appearances for the French club, scoring seven goals and providing 11 assists before joining PSG in August 2023.
He made 49 appearances for PSG last season, scoring 13 goals and registering seven assists.
The forward has also established himself as a France international since making his debut in June 2024. He has won 28 caps and scored six goals, including three during this summer's World Cup, where he featured in every match as France finished fourth.
At Liverpool, he becomes the club's third permanent signing of the summer after Víctor Muñoz and Jérémy Jacquet, while Ronald Araújo has also arrived from Barcelona on a season-long loan.
Barcola's arrival also comes with uncertainty around Cody Gakpo, with Manchester City having made an approach for the Liverpool forward. ESPN sources say Liverpool are unlikely to make another first-team signing before Tuesday's transfer deadline unless there are further departures, although Gakpo's exit would require the club to find a suitable replacement.
For now, Liverpool have secured one of Europe's most sought-after young forwards, with Barcola arriving at Anfield determined to turn a long-awaited transfer into a new chapter of his career.

briefs.headline: Argentina president Milei joins tributes to Messi, calls him an ‘impossible man’
briefs.deck: Lionel Messi’s international retirement has prompted tributes across Argentina, including an emotional message from President Javier Milei. After 207 appearances and 125 goals, Messi leaves the national team following a 21-year career featuring a World Cup and two Copa América titles. The 39-year-old will continue playing for Inter Miami, but his Argentina chapter is now over.
briefs.bodyText:
Lionel Messi’s decision to end his international career has prompted an emotional reaction across Argentina, with President Javier Milei among those paying tribute to the captain who delivered some of the greatest moments in the country’s football history.
Messi announced on Monday that he had decided to retire from international football following a period of reflection after Argentina’s defeat to Spain in the 2026 World Cup final. The decision brought an end to a remarkable international career spanning six World Cups, 207 appearances and 125 goals for his country.
Javier Milei pays tribute to Argentina’s captain
Argentina President Javier Milei was among the first prominent figures to respond to Messi’s announcement.
Sharing a photograph of the forward greeting supporters on Instagram, Milei wrote: “Muchas gracias HOMBRE IMPOSIBLE...!!!”
The message roughly translates to: “Thank you very much, impossible man.”
Milei’s tribute reflected the significance of Messi’s contribution to Argentine football, particularly after the forward helped end years of disappointment with the national team.
Messi admitted the decision was painful
Messi’s announcement came more than a month after Argentina’s 1-0 defeat to Spain in the 2026 World Cup final at MetLife Stadium on July 19, a result that left the 39-year-old with another World Cup final defeat to add to his international story.
The decision also arrived just weeks after Messi’s father, Jorge Messi, died on August 8 in Rosario at the age of 68, adding another deeply personal dimension to an already difficult period for the Argentina captain.
Messi confirmed his international retirement through an emotional statement on Instagram, explaining that he had reached the point where he felt he had nothing more to give while also acknowledging the emergence of a younger generation within the national team.
“After all this time since the final match, and after long reflection, I want to announce to everyone that I have decided to retire from playing with the national team,” Messi said.
“It was a painful decision and it still hurts me deep down, but I realise that the time has come.”
Argentina's Lionel Messi (10) reacts after the World Cup final soccer match between Spain and Argentina in East Rutherford, N.J., near New York, Sunday, July 19, 2026. (AP Photo/Stephanie Scarbrough)
The Argentina captain stressed that his commitment to the national team had never wavered throughout his career, including during the years when major international success repeatedly eluded him.
“I swear to you that I always gave everything I had, not only during the recent years in which we achieved everything, but before that too, and I always fought and gave all I had for this shirt, and to make you happy and make you feel proud to be Argentine through football,” he added.
Messi also acknowledged that the arrival of younger players had helped convince him that the time was right to step aside.
“I have exhausted everything I have, and I no longer have any more to give, alongside the presence of a group of wonderful young players who deserve to get their chance,” he said.
Messi’s Argentina career eventually became a story of redemption
Messi’s relationship with the Argentina national team was not always defined by the success that eventually came towards the end of his career.
The forward suffered several major disappointments with his country, including defeat to Germany in the 2014 World Cup final and losses in consecutive Copa América finals before finally winning his first major senior international trophy at the 2021 Copa América.
That triumph ended Argentina’s 28-year wait for a major international title and marked the beginning of an extraordinary period for Messi and his country.
A year later, Messi captained Argentina to World Cup glory in Qatar, beating France on penalties after a thrilling final finished 3-3 following extra time.
Messi scored twice in that final and converted his penalty during the shootout, helping Argentina win the World Cup for the first time in 36 years and the third time in the country's history.
FILE - Argentina's Lionel Messi kisses the World Cup trophy after receiving the Golden Ball award for best player of the tournament during the awards ceremony after Argentina defeated France at the World Cup final in Lusail, Qatar, Dec. 18, 2022. (AP Photo/Natacha Pisarenko, File)
He then helped Argentina retain the Copa América in 2024 before leading the team to another World Cup final in 2026, where Spain ultimately denied them back-to-back titles.
Despite that final defeat, Messi leaves international football having achieved almost everything available to him with Argentina, including the World Cup, two Copa América titles and Olympic gold.
Messi leaves behind an extraordinary World Cup record
Messi's longevity at international level is perhaps best illustrated by the fact that he appeared at six different World Cups between 2006 and 2026.
Across those tournaments, he scored 21 goals in 34 appearances, placing him second on the all-time World Cup scoring list behind France captain Kylian Mbappé, who has moved ahead of him with 22 goals.
Messi had previously overtaken Germany legend Miroslav Klose's tally before Mbappé eventually claimed the record.
The 2026 tournament was another productive campaign for Messi individually, with the Argentina captain scoring eight goals and providing four assists.
His performances included his first World Cup hat-trick, which came against Algeria during the tournament, further adding to a collection of records that had grown throughout his international career.
By the time he announced his retirement, Messi had also established himself as Argentina's most-capped player and leading goalscorer, with 207 appearances and 125 goals according to the figures accompanying his retirement announcement.
He also finishes as the highest-scoring player in South American international football.
Messi will continue with Inter Miami
Although his international career is over, Messi has not announced his retirement from club football and will continue playing for Inter Miami in Major League Soccer.
The Argentine remains a central figure for the American club and underlined that status in spectacular fashion on August 30, scoring four goals and providing an assist for Luis Suárez in Inter Miami’s 7-1 victory over CF Montréal. Messi scored in the 40th, 52nd, 83rd and 90+6th minutes, completing his hat-trick with a chipped finish in the 83rd minute. The performance marked the 62nd hat-trick of his club career.
Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi celebrates after scoring his side's third goal during the second half of an MLS soccer match against CF Montreal, Saturday, Aug. 29, 2026, in Miami. (AP Photo/Rebecca Blackwell)
Inter Miami currently sit fourth in the MLS standings with 42 points from 22 matches, having recorded 12 wins, six draws and four defeats, leaving them 10 points behind Nashville SC.
For Argentina, however, a remarkable chapter has now closed.

briefs.headline: Piers Morgan claims Messi’s retirement at 39 proves Ronaldo is the GOAT
briefs.deck: Lionel Messi’s international retirement has reignited Piers Morgan’s long-running Cristiano Ronaldo GOAT argument. Morgan points to Ronaldo’s record 146 international goals, compared with Messi’s 125, as proof that Ronaldo is football’s greatest. Messi leaves Argentina with a World Cup, two Copa América titles and 125 goals, while Ronaldo continues chasing 1,000 career goals before retirement.
briefs.bodyText:
Lionel Messi’s decision to retire from international football has given 
Piers Morgan
 another opportunity to make his feelings about the greatest player debate unmistakably clear.
The Argentine icon announced on Monday that he would no longer represent his country, bringing an extraordinary 21-year international career to an end after 207 appearances and 125 goals. Messi leaves the Argentina setup as his country’s record appearance-maker and leading goalscorer, having finally transformed a career once defined by international disappointment into one of unprecedented success.
His decision came after a difficult period for the 39-year-old, both professionally and personally. Argentina had been defeated by Spain in the 2026 World Cup final, giving Messi a second World Cup final defeat after the loss to Germany in 2014. Just weeks later, his father, Jorge Messi, died at the age of 68.
For Morgan, however, Messi’s departure from the international stage did not simply mark the end of an era. It provided another reason to argue that Cristiano Ronaldo should be regarded as the greatest footballer in history.
The broadcaster pointed towards Ronaldo’s record 146 international goals for Portugal and declared that Messi’s retirement had effectively settled the long-running argument in his friend’s favour.
Piers Morgan used Messi’s retirement to make his Ronaldo argument
Morgan has never been particularly shy about where he stands in the debate between Ronaldo and Messi, and his reaction to Monday’s announcement was therefore unlikely to pass without comment.
The British broadcaster has previously made his position clear by leaving Messi out of his all-time XI, despite the Argentine’s record eight Ballon d’Or wins and extraordinary list of team honours.
Morgan has also named four players he believes were better than Messi, making his view on the GOAT debate even clearer.
The British broadcaster first acknowledged Messi’s international scoring record before immediately drawing attention to Ronaldo’s superior tally for Portugal.
“Breaking: Lionel Messi retires from international football, after scoring 125 goals for the Argentina national team, placing him second on the list of highest international goalscorers,” Morgan wrote on X.
He then followed up by highlighting Ronaldo’s record for Portugal.
“Cristiano Ronaldo has scored 146 goals for the Portugal national team, the highest figure in the history of football at international level. This settles the debate over who is the best player in history,” he added.
It was hardly a neutral assessment, particularly given Morgan's well-known friendship with Ronaldo, but it quickly attracted attention because Messi's retirement has once again placed the two careers under the microscope.
Ronaldo has scored 146 goals for Portugal, while Messi finished his Argentina career with 125 goals, leaving the Portuguese forward 21 goals clear at international level. Ronaldo's record is also particularly significant because he has remained the leading men's international goalscorer while continuing to play for Portugal at the highest level.
Morgan's argument, however, reduces one of football's most complicated debates to a single statistical comparison, while Messi's international career offers plenty of evidence for those who disagree with him.
Messi leaves Argentina with a legacy that was once difficult to imagine
When Messi's international career began in 2005, his relationship with Argentina was far more complicated than the numbers he eventually produced might suggest.
The forward experienced repeated heartbreak with his country, most notably losing the 2014 World Cup final and suffering defeats in successive Copa América finals before finally winning his first senior international major trophy at the 2021 Copa América.
That breakthrough changed everything.
Messi subsequently captained Argentina to victory at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, completing the achievement that had eluded him for much of his career. He then added another Copa América title in 2024 before leading Argentina back to the World Cup final in 2026.
The 2026 tournament ultimately ended in disappointment, with Argentina losing the final to Spain, but Messi still departed the international stage with a résumé that includes a World Cup, two Copa América titles and an Olympic gold medal.
FILE - Argentina's Lionel Messi cries at the end of the World Cup final soccer match with Spain in East Rutherford, N.J., near New York, July 19, 2026. (AP Photo/Stephanie Scarbrough, File)
He also finished as Argentina's record appearance-maker and scorer, with his 125 goals coming across 207 appearances.
His final appearance came against Spain in the 2026 World Cup final, after which he took several weeks to consider his future before confirming that he would no longer play for Argentina.
Messi explained that the decision was painful but said he felt the time had arrived to step away.
“After all this time since the final match, and after long reflection, I want to announce to everyone that I have decided to retire from playing with the national team,” Messi wrote in a statement on Instagram.
“It was a painful decision and it still hurts me deep down, but I realise that the time has come. I swear to you that I always gave everything I had, not only during the recent years in which we achieved everything, but before that too.”
Messi added that he had always fought to represent Argentina and to make supporters proud.
“I always fought and gave all I had for this shirt, and to make you happy and make you feel proud to be Argentine through football,” he wrote.
In a further reflection on his decision, Messi admitted that he felt his time with the national team was coming to an end.
“There isn’t much time left, and different chapters are coming to an end. This is one that hurts me a lot,” he said. “I love, I loved, and I will always love being part of the national team. I gave everything I had, and I don’t have anything more to give.”
Ronaldo is chasing a career milestone Messi never reached
Ronaldo’s international record is only one part of the statistical case Morgan believes separates him from Messi.
The Portugal captain is also closing in on one of football’s most remarkable individual milestones: 1,000 senior career goals.
Ronaldo has already scored more than 900 goals for club and country, and his continued involvement with Al-Nassr and Portugal gives him a realistic opportunity to reach four figures before retiring. At 41, he remains one of the most prolific forwards in the game, even as his role and playing time continue to evolve.
The milestone has become a central part of the final chapter of Ronaldo’s career. Rather than simply trying to extend his longevity, he is now pursuing a record that would place him in an almost entirely separate statistical category.
Ronaldo recently gave his clearest indication yet that retirement is approaching, saying that the upcoming season is “probably” his final year of football and that he wants to leave what he described as a spectacular legacy.
That creates a clear contrast between the two rivals. Messi has ended his international career after completing his redemption story with Argentina, while Ronaldo is still chasing one last record that could define how his career is remembered.
Cristiano Ronaldo has now scored 978 official senior career goals in 1,333 games, leaving him just 22 goals short of the 1,000-goal milestone. By comparison, the 39-year-old Messi has scored 927 official senior career goals for club and country in 1,171 matches.
The numbers tell an interesting story. Ronaldo has the higher total and more international goals, while Messi has reached his tally in fewer matches.
Whether reaching 1,000 goals would settle the GOAT debate is another question entirely, but it would add another extraordinary achievement to an already historic career.
For Morgan, though, Ronaldo’s international scoring record, longevity and pursuit of that unprecedented total provide more than enough evidence.
Messi’s retirement may have closed one chapter of the rivalry, but Ronaldo’s numbers suggest that the argument will continue until the final goal of his career is scored.

briefs.headline: 'All the joy he gave us': Argentines thank Messi as he announces international retirement
briefs.deck: It’s going ​to be difficult, but I’m super grateful ⁠for all the joy he gave us, as a country, says Francisca Mieth, an 18-year-old university student, in Buenos Aires' leafy Belgrano neighbourhood
briefs.bodyText:
Argentines saluted Lionel Messi on Monday (August 31, 2026) after the soccer great confirmed the news many had long expected but still found painful: his retirement from the national team.
“It’s going to be difficult, but I’m super grateful for all the joy he gave us, as a country,” said Francisca Mieth, an 18-year-old university student, in Buenos Aires' leafy Belgrano neighbourhood.
Nearby, dog walker Jose Aramburu said Messi’s refusal to give up had left a lasting mark on Argentina.
“The most important thing that Messi gave us was the fact that he insisted, persisted and pursued a dream, a goal, an objective, without caring about what other people said,” the 36-year-old said.
Messi, 39, who captained Argentina to World Cup glory in 2022 and another final in 2026, announced his international retirement on Instagram on Monday, describing it as "a decision that hurts the soul."
His image had been inescapable during this year's World Cup, appearing on billboards across downtown Buenos Aires and towering over a Patagonian town in the form of an 85-foot statue.
Locals there watched Argentina play England on a screen erected beside the statue's giant knees.
As Messi broke records with his scoring streak during the tournament, Argentines took to the streets to sing "Happy Birthday" when he turned 39 in June.
Messi said that the death of his father in August after a long illness had cemented his decision to end his international career.
"The end of an era," read a headline on the website of Argentine newspaper La Nacion.
A psychologist interviewed on local television channel TN cautioned against expecting another player to fill the void, saying "no one should be burdened with the weight of being his replacement."
Meanwhile, praise poured in on social media from Messi's former teammates, including Angel Di Maria, who retired from international football in 2024.
"We're going to be grateful to you for our entire lives for being Argentine," he wrote.

briefs.headline: Athletics | Nobody can take away the piece of history I achieved: Chukwuebuka Enekwechi
briefs.deck: The 33-year-old stresses he wants to stay consistent at the top level before his decline; says Nigerian throwers are grappling with infrastructure and funding issues
briefs.bodyText:
Chukwuebuka Enekwechi presents a fine example of how perseverance can reward an athlete. Despite funding issues, the Nigerian lived in the USA for years to pursue his studies and shot put career before ultimately writing a bit of sporting history. He became the first shot putter from his country to win gold at the Commonwealth Games, achieving the feat in Glasgow.
It was a moment of immense pride for the 33-year-old as he recorded a mark of 21.07m and pipped one of his idols, New Zealand’s Worlds and Olympic medallist Tom Walsh. Fresh from his CWG glory, Enekwechi, who hails from the Anambra State, lived up to his billing by securing the top place with 20.78m at the World Athletics Continental Tour Silver meet at the Kalinga Stadium in Bhubaneswar.
During an interaction, he spoke about his journey, ambitions and experience of competing in India.
How did you feel after becoming Nigeria’s first shot putter to win gold at the Commonwealth Games?
It was amazing, especially at that moment. My life hasn’t changed much, but it was a piece of history. It was a huge honour. Many people tried before me and came close. For me to be the first person in history, it’s something that nobody can take away from me. And I made a lot of people proud and happy. That means the world to me.
You had clinched a silver in the 2018 CWG. What happened after that?
It was eight years ago. A lot can change in one year. I tried to get a medal in Birmingham (2022) but I didn’t. I was fourth. The pressure doubled leading up to Glasgow. But I knew I had to stay consistent, work hard and take it extremely seriously. I prepared very well, but I was also a bit lucky to have that win. So I’m very grateful.
How did you get into shot put?
I just wanted to lift weights and I had to do something. I had to join a team to lift weights. So I joined athletics on a whim, and things just kept getting better and better.
What challenges do Nigerian throwers face?
It’s mostly infrastructure issues. A lot of the attention goes towards sprints and events that already have funding from shoe companies. The throws (events) don’t get much funding. That would make a big difference... some of it is like investing in coaching and facilities.
The other thing is that I’ve had a lot of international success. Maybe leaning into that, positioning me in a position where I can help out some of the young guys coming up. That would be a very big benefit for the nation.
Where do you train and how is the funding now?
Funding... it’s not there. But I train in Lafayette, Indiana (USA). I went to school at Purdue University and that’s where I train now. I moved there for schooling and after I graduated, I just stayed there and continued to train. I’m 10 years out of school, so I’ve been there for 15 years now.
What advice will you give to young Nigerian throwers?
Give yourself a chance because when you look at me, I’m not the biggest thrower. I’m probably the shortest guy in the field: I’m 180 centimetres tall. And if you looked at me, especially before I put on a lot of muscle, you would not have thought of me as world-class or as a 22-metre shot putter. But I took a chance on myself and I was able to execute it. What it means is that many more kids can do what I did or even better.
Do you get the opportunity to go back to Nigeria?
Yeah, I go to Nigeria once or twice every year... for the National championships, for the sports festival. I take that opportunity to coach some of the local talent. Just kind of give them advice, give the coaches advice... just like there’s so much support for the Indian talent. That’s how I feel for my countrymen. I want them to succeed just as much as anybody would for their country. I do as much as I can to help.
What’s your next goal?
I would love to get another major medal and improve my personal best. I’m 33 years old now, but every year I seem to find something new to add to my repertoire. I just want to keep improving. Before I start to decline, I just want to be consistent at a high level.
Do you have anything specific in mind?
I want to keep making finals and compete for a medal at major championships. That would be awesome.
Who are your inspirations?
Some of the guys who are still competing. I looked up to Joe Kovacs for a long time. He’s one of the throwers who’s not the biggest but super powerful and consistent. I followed him and added my own stuff to get to a world-class level.
And the funny thing is I’m like that for some younger throwers now. It’s kind of full circle. Joe was a big inspiration for me... Reese Hoffa, Ryan Whiting and Adam Nelson. A lot of the guys who are still involved in the sport... even Walsh. We’re not that different in terms of age, but he was achieving at such a high level when I was still in university. These guys are friends now. But I looked up to them and I kind of learned from them.
Have you made some Indian friends?
Yeah. I met two of the local guys. I’ve known Tajinderpal Singh Toor for years now. I just met Samardeep Gill in Glasgow. In shot put, we’re all competitors but we’re also colleagues. So there’s always respect in the first place. I know the guys were cheering each other on in between rounds. Even though we compete hard, there’s a lot of support within the group.
How was the experience of coming to India and competing here?
It was very nice. One thing I can tell about India is that Indians are very proud of their culture. We had a good immersive experience. The music, meeting some of the dignitaries, the art styles, culture, food. We were immersed in the culture. I’ve been at it for 10 years now. This is my first time in India. New experiences are always welcome. I had a lot of fun.

briefs.headline: Lionel Messi announces retirement from international football
briefs.deck: "It was a decision that hurt and still hurts deep in my soul but I understand that it is the right time," Messi, 39, wrote on Instagram.
briefs.bodyText:
Lionel Messi said on Monday (August 31, 2026) he is retiring from international football after leading Argentina to a second successive World Cup final in July.
"It was a decision that hurt and still hurts deep in my soul but I understand that it is the right time," Messi, 39, wrote on Instagram.
“I swear I always gave everything, not just in the last few years when we won everything but before that too, and I always fought and gave my all for this shirt,” he added.
Messi led Argentina to World Cup glory by winning the 2022 final against France in a penalty shootout in Doha, but his side lost 1-0 to Spain in the 2026 final.
Following the death of his father Jorge on August 8, 2026, Messi had said he had “serious doubts” about continuing to play football of any sort for “much longer”.
Messi’s contract with Major League Soccer club Inter Miami runs until the end of the 2028 season.

briefs.headline: VIS-The Hindu u-15 inter-school tournament inaugurated
briefs.bodyText:
Sports Bureau
Chennai: Vellore International School (VIS), Chennai, and The Hindu inaugurated the third edition of the under-15 inter-school football tournament at the VIS campus in Kayar on Monday.
The tournament features 64 school teams from Chennai, Kancheepuram, Tiruvallur, Vellore, Chengalpattu and Tiruvannamalai.

Selvam (vice-president, Vellore Institute of Technology, and chairman, VIS), K. Prabhakaran (principal, VIS), Rohit Ramesh (director, The Hindu Group) and L.V. Navaneeth (CEO, The Hindu Group).
Speaking at the inauguration, Rohit Ramesh said, “We, at The Hindu, believe that journalism isn’t just about reporting the news; it’s about supporting the stories that build our community. Sports is one of the most powerful vehicles for that. It teaches discipline, resilience and the value of teamwork — lessons that go far beyond the football field.”
The tournament was officially declared open by Korenaga, who kicked off the opening match between KC High International School and P.A.K. Palanisamy Higher Secondary School.

briefs.headline: Chennai Bulls reigns supreme in the Equestrian CL
briefs.deck: Bangalore Knights (291) and Golconda Chargers (Telangana, 286) were in the hunt for the title for the most part before the Bulls performed one better to wear the crown
briefs.bodyText:
Chennai Bulls, representing Tamil Nadu, tallied 311 points for the top spot and the champions tag in the national-level Equestrian Champions League (ECL) at an arena near the Equestrian Crest in Molapalayam on Sunday (August 31, 2026).
Bangalore Knights (291) and Golconda Chargers (Telangana, 286) were in the hunt for the title for the most part before the Bulls performed one better to wear the crown. The team went home richer by ₹15 lakhs as well, while Bangalore Knights and Golconda Chargers had to rest content with a cash purse of ₹10 lakhs and five lakhs respectively.
A. Raja, Member of Parliament, Nilgiris Constituency, gave away the prizes. K.A. Sengottaiyan, Minister for Revenue and Disaster Management, MLA Sathyabama, actors Arya and Shyam, Sundar Ramakrishnan, Managing Trustee, SNR Sons Charitable Trust, A.S. Sakti Balaji, President, Equestrian Champions League, were also present.
